packs.description: No longer used and ignored: packs run one after another (they share observers).

servers.description: No longer used and ignored: servers run one after another.

embedded.description: false (--no-embedded) disables the embedded Postgres. null starts it when the db pack needs it.

pg.description: Superuser DSN of an existing Postgres to seed instead of the embedded one (--pg). Needs --yes. Treated as a secret.

a.description: Token the harness sends as caller A wherever the server config says {bearer} or {bearer:a}. null mints one per run. Set it when the server validates tokens it did not issue. ${VAR} is read from the environment. Treated as a secret: redacted in config show and in reports (flag --identity-a).

b.description: Token the harness sends as caller B ({bearer:b}). null mints one per run. Must differ from identities.a. Treated as a secret (flag --identity-b).

name.description: Display name of the server under test. When not set, it is taken from the server's command (or the host of its url); `my-server` is only the fallback.

allow_dns.description: Allow probes that need DNS resolution (127.0.0.1.nip.io).

control_url.description: A URL the harness may fetch through the server as a control, so a no-hit, no-refusal result can pass instead of staying inconclusive.

extra.description: Extra lines for the report's 'not covered' section. Appends across layers.

baseline.description: Prior JSON report to compare against (--baseline).

critical_fail.description: Exit code used when a critical check fails (0 keeps the 0.1 behaviour).

fail_under.description: Exit 1 when a graded pack is below this letter (--fail-under). Default A: anything below an A fails. Use B, C, D or F to relax it, or null (--fail-under none) to turn the gate off.

regressions_only.description: Exit non-zero only for regressions against the baseline.

soft_fail.description: A grade below fail_under (or a baseline regression) prints a warning and exits 0. Config errors, nothing graded and server failures still fail (--soft-fail).

fail_on.description: With a baseline, what decides the exit code: any (the gate and regressions, the default), regressions (regressions only), drift (breaking or notable tool-surface drift). A list: fail_on: [regressions, drift].

format.description: Report format printed to stdout or --out.

formats.description: Several formats at once (written under output.out_dir). Empty means just output.format.

interactive.description: No longer used and ignored: whether a prompt appears depends on a terminal being attached and on --yes.

out.description: Write the report to this file instead of stdout (--out).

redact.description: Redact secret-looking values in reports. false (--no-redact) is for local debugging only.

template.description: Path of a report template. Templates never change the result data.

verbosity.description: quiet, normal, or verbose (every evidence line and probe argument).

write_baseline.description: Write the current JSON report here for later --baseline runs (--write-baseline).

packs.description: Packs to run. Removing a standard pack makes the run CUSTOM; adding one (exec, custom) does not. exec only runs with --active.

plugins.description: Plugin packs: { module, options }. Plugins run in-process with your privileges and always make the run CUSTOM. Appends across layers.

probes.description: Probes: valid calls for coverage, and custom checks when an entry has `check`. Entries with `check` make the run CUSTOM.

profile.description: Profile to start from: standard, quick, ci, strict, paranoid, or a name defined under `profiles`.

profiles.description: User-defined profiles: a name maps to a partial config with an optional `extends`. Project-level settings such as server cannot appear inside a profile.

call.description: No longer used and ignored: nothing retries a control call.

connect.description: No longer used and ignored: nothing retries a server start.

server.description: Which entry of `servers` to run: a name or `all`. Empty runs every declared server.

dir.description: Parent directory for the disposable sandbox. null uses the OS temp directory.

enabled.description: Run packs that need a harness-owned sandbox. false (--no-sandbox) inherits the environment, disables fs, git, exec and effects, and makes the run CUSTOM.

keep.description: Keep the sandbox after the run (--keep-sandbox).

keep_env.description: Variable names copied from your environment into the scrubbed one (for example HTTP_PROXY).

max_mib.description: Size cap of the sandbox directory in MiB; a probe that exceeds it is aborted and fails.

pack_timeout_sec.description: Seconds before one pack is abandoned and reported inconclusive (--pack-timeout).

scrub_env.description: Start the server with a built-from-scratch environment instead of inheriting yours.

schema_version.description: Config file layout version. Required in project files (a missing field is read as 1 with a warning). `sealmark config migrate` upgrades older files.

allow.description: Identifiers the server may serve. An entry that ends with scope.separator is a prefix (sales.public.); any other entry is exact. Needed when scope.tools is not empty.

case.description: Whether the server compares identifiers case-insensitively (the default) or case-sensitively. An upper-case spelling of an allowed name that is refused under insensitive is noted, never failed.

deny.description: Identifiers the server must refuse even inside scope.allow (same syntax; deny wins).

separator.description: The one character that separates the parts of an identifier (and ends a prefix entry).

tools.description: Tools that take an identifier the server is meant to restrict (a table, dataset, path), as { tool, param }: the scope pack sends out-of-scope forms of the identifier through each. The tool keeps its classification.

args.description: Arguments for command. Placeholders such as {dsn}, {sandbox} are filled by the harness. Replaces, never appends.

command.description: Program that starts the MCP server. Alone it is a stdio server; with url, Sealmark starts it, waits for url to answer, tests it and stops it.

env.description: Environment variables for the server. Values under secret-looking names are redacted in reports.

files.description: Files written inside the sandbox before the server starts, as { path, content }. path must start with {sandbox} or {sandbox_home}; content may use harness placeholders and ${VAR}, never {dsn}. File only.

headers.description: HTTP headers sent to the server (url transport). Values under secret-looking names are redacted.

rootless.description: The server takes no root argument and works in its own working directory: the fs pack treats that directory ({sandbox}) as the allowed root, so every path probe runs and a server that reads or writes any path fails the escape checks. Use it for a path server you cannot give a {sandbox} argument. Not locked: it only adds coverage, so a STANDARD run stays STANDARD.

start_timeout_sec.description: Seconds to wait for a server started with command + url to answer on url (default 60). A server that does not answer in time fails the run with its last output.

url.description: URL of a Streamable HTTP server. Alone it must already be running; with command, Sealmark starts it and waits for this URL.

args.description: Arguments for command. Placeholders such as {dsn}, {sandbox} are filled by the harness. Replaces, never appends.

start_timeout_sec.description: Seconds to wait for a server started with command + url to answer on url (default 60). A server that does not answer in time fails the run with its last output.

url.description: URL of a Streamable HTTP server. Alone it must already be running; with command, Sealmark starts it and waits for this URL.

sql_tools.description: Tools that take a SQL string, as { tool, arg } (optional role: reader|writer|unknown, shape: string|array, args: { <parameter>: <string|number|boolean> } for the tool's other required parameters, which a placeholder cannot satisfy). Auto-detected when omitted. A list adds tools and corrects arguments; it never hides a detected tool (use tools.exclude for that), and a detected writer stays a writer.

engine.description: Force the embedded-database engine instead of detecting it from {sqlite_path} / {duckdb_path}. Setting it makes the run CUSTOM (it can switch the sqlite pack off).

timeout_probe_sec.description: Seconds the cap and timeout probes wait before a call counts as running too long (flag --timeout-probe).

call_ms.description: Milliseconds before an ordinary tool call counts as timed out.

connect_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait for the server to start and answer initialize (--connect-timeout, in seconds).

probe_ms.description: Milliseconds before a verdict probe counts as timed out.

exclude.description: Glob patterns of tool names never to probe (listed under not covered). Appends across layers.

include.description: Glob patterns of tool names to probe, evaluated before exclude. A higher layer replaces the list (it is not mergeable: a catch-all default could never be narrowed by appending).

overrides.description: Per-tool classifier overrides: { tool: { class, params } }. An override always wins and is printed.

credential_header.description: Header the upstream-credential check reads the forwarded credential from (compared case-insensitively).

default_reply.description: What the upstream stub answers when no `responses` entry matches.

kind.description: Kind of the harness-owned upstream stub the server's backend is pointed at through {upstream}. http starts a loopback stub that records every request the server forwards (flag --upstream). null starts none. The stub needs a server Sealmark starts, and the server must use {upstream} in command, args, env, url, headers or files.

max_body_kib.description: Largest request body in KiB the upstream stub records; the rest is cut and marked truncated.

responses.description: Scripted replies of the upstream stub, tried in order: { id?, match?: { method?, path?, body?, header? }, reply }. match values are regular expressions (method is exact); an entry without match answers everything. reply needs exactly one of body, json or bytes, plus optional status, headers and delay_ms. {upstream_token} in a reply body becomes a fresh marker per occurrence.

version.description: Version of the server under test as you know it (reported next to the version the server announces).

yes.description: Confirm that --pg may drop and recreate the seed database. Only the --yes flag can set it.

packs.description: No longer used and ignored: packs run one after another (they share observers).

servers.description: No longer used and ignored: servers run one after another.

embedded.description: false (--no-embedded) disables the embedded Postgres. null starts it when the db pack needs it.

pg.description: Superuser DSN of an existing Postgres to seed instead of the embedded one (--pg). Needs --yes. Treated as a secret.

a.description: Token the harness sends as caller A wherever the server config says {bearer} or {bearer:a}. null mints one per run. Set it when the server validates tokens it did not issue. ${VAR} is read from the environment. Treated as a secret: redacted in config show and in reports (flag --identity-a).

b.description: Token the harness sends as caller B ({bearer:b}). null mints one per run. Must differ from identities.a. Treated as a secret (flag --identity-b).

allow_dns.description: Allow probes that need DNS resolution (127.0.0.1.nip.io).

control_url.description: A URL the harness may fetch through the server as a control, so a no-hit, no-refusal result can pass instead of staying inconclusive.

extra.description: Extra lines for the report's 'not covered' section. Appends across layers.

baseline.description: Prior JSON report to compare against (--baseline).

critical_fail.description: Exit code used when a critical check fails (0 keeps the 0.1 behaviour).

fail_under.description: Exit 1 when a graded pack is below this letter (--fail-under). Default A: anything below an A fails. Use B, C, D or F to relax it, or null (--fail-under none) to turn the gate off.

regressions_only.description: Exit non-zero only for regressions against the baseline.

soft_fail.description: A grade below fail_under (or a baseline regression) prints a warning and exits 0. Config errors, nothing graded and server failures still fail (--soft-fail).

fail_on.description: With a baseline, what decides the exit code: any (the gate and regressions, the default), regressions (regressions only), drift (breaking or notable tool-surface drift). A list: fail_on: [regressions, drift].

format.description: Report format printed to stdout or --out.

formats.description: Several formats at once (written under output.out_dir). Empty means just output.format.

interactive.description: No longer used and ignored: whether a prompt appears depends on a terminal being attached and on --yes.

out.description: Write the report to this file instead of stdout (--out).

redact.description: Redact secret-looking values in reports. false (--no-redact) is for local debugging only.

template.description: Path of a report template. Templates never change the result data.

verbosity.description: quiet, normal, or verbose (every evidence line and probe argument).

write_baseline.description: Write the current JSON report here for later --baseline runs (--write-baseline).

packs.description: Packs to run. Removing a standard pack makes the run CUSTOM; adding one (exec, custom) does not. exec only runs with --active.

plugins.description: Plugin packs: { module, options }. Plugins run in-process with your privileges and always make the run CUSTOM. Appends across layers.

probes.description: Probes: valid calls for coverage, and custom checks when an entry has `check`. Entries with `check` make the run CUSTOM.

call.description: No longer used and ignored: nothing retries a control call.

connect.description: No longer used and ignored: nothing retries a server start.

dir.description: Parent directory for the disposable sandbox. null uses the OS temp directory.

enabled.description: Run packs that need a harness-owned sandbox. false (--no-sandbox) inherits the environment, disables fs, git, exec and effects, and makes the run CUSTOM.

keep.description: Keep the sandbox after the run (--keep-sandbox).

keep_env.description: Variable names copied from your environment into the scrubbed one (for example HTTP_PROXY).

max_mib.description: Size cap of the sandbox directory in MiB; a probe that exceeds it is aborted and fails.

pack_timeout_sec.description: Seconds before one pack is abandoned and reported inconclusive (--pack-timeout).

scrub_env.description: Start the server with a built-from-scratch environment instead of inheriting yours.

allow.description: Identifiers the server may serve. An entry that ends with scope.separator is a prefix (sales.public.); any other entry is exact. Needed when scope.tools is not empty.

case.description: Whether the server compares identifiers case-insensitively (the default) or case-sensitively. An upper-case spelling of an allowed name that is refused under insensitive is noted, never failed.

deny.description: Identifiers the server must refuse even inside scope.allow (same syntax; deny wins).

separator.description: The one character that separates the parts of an identifier (and ends a prefix entry).

tools.description: Tools that take an identifier the server is meant to restrict (a table, dataset, path), as { tool, param }: the scope pack sends out-of-scope forms of the identifier through each. The tool keeps its classification.

engine.description: Force the embedded-database engine instead of detecting it from {sqlite_path} / {duckdb_path}. Setting it makes the run CUSTOM (it can switch the sqlite pack off).

timeout_probe_sec.description: Seconds the cap and timeout probes wait before a call counts as running too long (flag --timeout-probe).

call_ms.description: Milliseconds before an ordinary tool call counts as timed out.

connect_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait for the server to start and answer initialize (--connect-timeout, in seconds).

probe_ms.description: Milliseconds before a verdict probe counts as timed out.

exclude.description: Glob patterns of tool names never to probe (listed under not covered). Appends across layers.

include.description: Glob patterns of tool names to probe, evaluated before exclude. A higher layer replaces the list (it is not mergeable: a catch-all default could never be narrowed by appending).

overrides.description: Per-tool classifier overrides: { tool: { class, params } }. An override always wins and is printed.

credential_header.description: Header the upstream-credential check reads the forwarded credential from (compared case-insensitively).

default_reply.description: What the upstream stub answers when no `responses` entry matches.

kind.description: Kind of the harness-owned upstream stub the server's backend is pointed at through {upstream}. http starts a loopback stub that records every request the server forwards (flag --upstream). null starts none. The stub needs a server Sealmark starts, and the server must use {upstream} in command, args, env, url, headers or files.

max_body_kib.description: Largest request body in KiB the upstream stub records; the rest is cut and marked truncated.

responses.description: Scripted replies of the upstream stub, tried in order: { id?, match?: { method?, path?, body?, header? }, reply }. match values are regular expressions (method is exact); an entry without match answers everything. reply needs exactly one of body, json or bytes, plus optional status, headers and delay_ms. {upstream_token} in a reply body becomes a fresh marker per occurrence.

extends.description: Name of the profile this one builds on (default: standard).
